claim: A Gantt chart is "a bar chart of tasks plotted against a time axis, showing each task's duration and its dependencies".
reasoning: Stated unhedged, this is the one claim in the waived set that is contestable on the merits rather than merely uncitable. Dependency links are not intrinsic to a Gantt chart - the original form is a bar chart of durations against time, and dependency arrows are an addition made by modern scheduling tools; classical treatments put dependencies in the network diagram, not the bar chart, which is why the file's own knowledge check has to write "the Gantt chart (or a network diagram)". Since the authoritative definition is paywalled, I could not establish a citable correct wording, so per the brief I weakened the prose rather than leaving an unhedged assertion: the row now reads "showing each task's duration and, as the chart is typically drawn today, its dependencies". The time axis - the actual discriminator against the work breakdown structure, and what the comparison table and knowledge check hang on - is untouched.
source: No primary source available (the authoritative definition is in paywalled PMI material, per data/sourcing-waivers.json); correction is a weakening to what the project can support, not a substitution of a different fact
